title: Curve testing for geometric irreducibility
statement:
Let $X_0$ be a smooth, geometrically connected, affine scheme of
relative dimension $d\geq1$ over a finite field $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, with
$X=X_0\times_{k_0}\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, and let
$\mathcal S_1,\ldots,\mathcal S_r$ be $\Qlb$-Weil sheaves on $X_0$ whose
geometric restrictions to $X$ are irreducible local systems. Let $S$ be
a nonempty finite set of $\overline{\mathbf F}_q$-points of $X$. There
are a smooth connected affine curve $C$ over $\overline{\mathbf F}_q$
and a closed immersion $i:C\hookrightarrow X$ whose image contains $S$,
such that every $i^*\mathcal S_j$ is an irreducible local system on $C$,
and $C$ is defined over a finite extension $\mathbf F_{q^m}$, $m\ge1$:
there is an automorphism $\varphi$ of $C$ with
$i\circ\varphi=(\mathrm{id}_{X_0}\times\sigma)^m\circ i$, where
$\mathrm{id}_{X_0}\times\sigma$ is the geometric Galois Frobenius of
$X$.

proof.text: For $d\geq2$, choose $s\in S$ and use $\bar x=s$ as geometric base point. Apply [lem-zl-common-irreducibility-detecting-cover] to the geometric local systems on $X$. Here $X$ is connected by geometric connectedness, and is Noetherian and separated since it is affine of finite type over $\overline{\mathbf F}_q$; $\ell$ is invertible. Obtain $q:\pi_1(X,\bar x)\twoheadrightarrow Q$ and a connected finite etale $T\to X$ with fibre the regular $Q$-set. Any subgroup surjecting onto $Q$ acts irreducibly on every geometric stalk.

source.place: proof, finite representations, matrix witnesses and common quotient cover

proof.text: Apply [lem-zl-bertini-finite-cover-curve] to $X_0,T\to X,S$: smoothness, affineness, geometric connectedness and $d\geq2$ are the hypotheses, and $T$ is connected. Obtain $i:C\hookrightarrow X$ through $S$, with $C$ smooth, connected and affine, $T\times_X C$ connected, and an automorphism $\varphi$ satisfying $i\circ\varphi=(\mathrm{id}_{X_0}\times\sigma)^m\circ i$ for some $m\geq1$.

source.place: proof, Bertini and finite-field descent sentences

proof.text: Since $C$ contains $s$, choose $\bar c$ with $i\bar c=s=\bar x$. By [lem-galois-finite-etale-connected-object], $T\times_XC$ is a connected finite-etale object. By [lem-galois-transitive] and base-change compatibility in [thm-galois-fundamental], $H=\operatorname{im}(i_*)$ acts transitively on $Q$ by left multiplication through $q$. Its orbit of $1$ is $q(H)$, so $q(H)=Q$.

source.place: proof, connected restricted torsor and transitive monodromy

proof.text: The detecting property of [lem-zl-common-irreducibility-detecting-cover] makes every geometric stalk representation irreducible on $H$. At each finite lattice level, [thm-galois-fundamental] identifies pullback fibres and their actions through $i_*$. Taking inverse limits, rationalizing and extending coefficients as in [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves] gives the action $\rho_j\circ i_*$ on the stalk of $i^*\mathcal S_j$. The exact equivalence [cor-galois-lisse-representations](2) now makes each pullback an irreducible local system.

source.place: proof, finite matrix conclusion and identification of restricted representations

proof.text: The automorphism $\varphi$ of $C$ with $i\circ\varphi=(\mathrm{id}_{X_0}\times\sigma)^m\circ i$, $m\geq1$, is the last conclusion of [lem-zl-bertini-finite-cover-curve] obtained in Step 2; this is the clause "$C$ is defined over $\mathbf F_{q^m}$" of the statement, no further finite-field model being asserted. (For the record: iterating the Weil datum $\Phi_X^*\mathcal S_j\cong\mathcal S_j$ of [def-wf-fundamental-representation] $m$ times and pulling it back along $i$, using $i\circ\varphi=\Phi_X^m\circ i$, gives $\varphi^*i^*\mathcal S_j\cong i^*\mathcal S_j$, the inherited Weil structure; the statement does not require it.)

source.place: proof, curve and inclusion descend and restrictions inherit Weil structures

proof.text: For $d=1$, take $C=X$, $i=\mathrm{id}_X$, $m=1$ and $\varphi=\mathrm{id}_{X_0}\times\sigma$. All restrictions are unchanged and every point of $S$ lies on $C$.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $X_0$ be a smooth, geometrically connected, affine scheme of
relative dimension $d\geq1$ over a finite field $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, with
$X=X_0\times_{k_0}\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, and let
$\mathcal S_1,\ldots,\mathcal S_r$ be $\Qlb$-Weil sheaves on $X_0$ whose
geometric restrictions to $X$ are irreducible local systems. Let $S$ be
a nonempty finite set of $\overline{\mathbf F}_q$-points of $X$. There
are a smooth connected affine curve $C$ over $\overline{\mathbf F}_q$
and a closed immersion $i:C\hookrightarrow X$ whose image contains $S$,
such that every $i^*\mathcal S_j$ is an irreducible local system on $C$,
and $C$ is defined over a finite extension $\mathbf F_{q^m}$, $m\ge1$:
there is an automorphism $\varphi$ of $C$ with
$i\circ\varphi=(\mathrm{id}_{X_0}\times\sigma)^m\circ i$, where
$\mathrm{id}_{X_0}\times\sigma$ is the geometric Galois Frobenius of
$X$.

proof.text:
Use the geometric representations of
[def-wf-fundamental-representation], and choose finite coefficient
fields for them as allowed in [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category].
By [lem-zl-finite-matrix-irreducibility], each has a finite
reduction quotient detecting absolute irreducibility. Intersect
their open normal kernels in $\pi_1(X)$, where
$X=X_0\times\overline{\mathbf F}_q$. The resulting finite quotient
$Q$ corresponds to a connected finite etale Galois cover $T\to X$.
For $\dim X\geq2$, apply
[lem-zl-bertini-finite-cover-curve]. Connectedness of the
restricted $Q$-torsor means that the image of $\pi_1(C)$ acts
transitively on $Q$, hence is all of $Q$. It surjects onto each
chosen reduction quotient. The finite matrix witnesses show that
all the restricted geometric representations remain irreducible.
The curve and inclusion descend to a finite constant extension;
the restrictions inherit their Weil structures over that field.
For dimension one take $C=X$, with its given finite-field model.
